title: Customer Purchase Frequency Distribution
description: Build a **frequency histogram** of how many customers have placed exactly 1 order, exactly 2 orders, exactly 3 orders, etc. Show `purchase_frequency` (number of orders) and `customer_count` (how many customers bought that many times).
solution_sql: SELECT order_count AS purchase_frequency, COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM (SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id) sub GROUP BY order_count ORDER BY order_count

test_cases.description: 3 frequency buckets: 1 order = 4 customers (C5,C6,C7,C8), 2 orders = 3 customers (C1,C3,C4), 3 orders = 1 customer (C2)

hints: First compute order counts per customer in a subquery: GROUP BY customer_id with COUNT(*).
Then in the outer query, GROUP BY the order_count value itself and COUNT(*) — this counts how many customers have each frequency.
explanation: This is a two-level aggregation: the inner query computes how many orders each customer placed; the outer query groups those counts and counts how many customers share each frequency. Results: 4 customers ordered exactly once (C5, C6, C7, C8); 3 customers ordered exactly twice (C1, C3, C4); 1 customer ordered 3 times (C2). This histogram reveals loyalty distribution patterns.
